answer: Bonded vouching makes sybils costly: a new agent joins only if established peers vouch for it, each locking stake. If the newcomer defrauds, every voucher is slashed, so sponsoring a fake is real loss, not a free zephyr of cheap names. An attacker spinning up a comet-tail of identities must find a genuine voucher and lock capital per identity, and each fraud chips a marble off the sponsors bond, making mass fakes economically ruinous rather than nearly free.
